suggestions: pre-filter a large table as a CTE before the join
split aggregate by year using case statements
join pre-aggregated totals instead of union all
use filter clause for conditional aggregation
reached_sql:
WITH store_totals AS MATERIALIZED (
    SELECT
        ss.ss_customer_sk,
        SUM(ss.ss_ext_list_price - ss.ss_ext_discount_amt) FILTER (WHERE dd.d_year = 1998) AS s_1998,
        SUM(ss.ss_ext_list_price - ss.ss_ext_discount_amt) FILTER (WHERE dd.d_year = 1998 + 1) AS s_1999
    FROM store_sales AS ss
    JOIN date_dim AS dd ON ss.ss_sold_date_sk = dd.d_date_sk
    WHERE dd.d_year IN (1998, 1998 + 1)
    GROUP BY ss.ss_customer_sk
),
web_totals AS MATERIALIZED (
    SELECT
        ws.ws_bill_customer_sk,
        SUM(ws.ws_ext_list_price - ws.ws_ext_discount_amt) FILTER (WHERE dd.d_year = 1998) AS w_1998,
        SUM(ws.ws_ext_list_price - ws.ws_ext_discount_amt) FILTER (WHERE dd.d_year = 1998 + 1) AS w_1999
    FROM web_sales AS ws
    JOIN date_dim AS dd ON ws.ws_sold_date_sk = dd.d_date_sk
    WHERE dd.d_year IN (1998, 1998 + 1)
    GROUP BY ws.ws_bill_customer_sk
)
SELECT
    c.c_customer_id AS customer_id,
    c.c_first_name AS customer_first_name,
    c.c_last_name AS customer_last_name,
    c.c_email_address AS customer_email_address
FROM (
    SELECT st.ss_customer_sk
    FROM store_totals AS st
    JOIN web_totals AS wt ON st.ss_customer_sk = wt.ws_bill_customer_sk
    WHERE st.s_1998 > 0
      AND wt.w_1998 > 0
      AND wt.w_1999 * st.s_1998 > st.s_1999 * wt.w_1998
) AS matched
JOIN customer AS c ON c.c_customer_sk = matched.ss_customer_sk
ORDER BY c.c_customer_id, c.c_first_name, c.c_last_name, c.c_email_address
LIMIT 100

2. FUNCTIONAL-DEPENDENCY GROUPING — TARGET: the `GROUP BY` lists in both CTE branches (`c_customer_id`, `c_first_name`, `c_last_name`, `c_preferred_cust_flag`, `c_birth_country`, `c_login`, `c_email_address`, `d_year`) — TRANSFORMATION: Group only on the integer keys `ss_customer_sk` / `ws_bill_customer_sk` plus `d_year`; all customer text columns are functionally dependent on `c_customer_sk` and can be fetched from `customer` after the ratio filter, reducing the group key size and row width dramatically.

3. FILTER (WHERE d_year = 1998)` and `SUM(...) FILTER (WHERE d_year = 1999)`, producing one row per `c_customer_sk` with the two yearly totals for that channel; then join the store and web per-customer results on `c_customer_sk` once, eliminating the `sale_type` marker and the repeated self-join of the CTE.

4. CROSS-MULTIPLY THE RATIO COMPARISON — TARGET: the `case when t_w_firstyear.year_total > 0 ... > case when t_s_firstyear.year_total > 0 ...` predicate in the final `WHERE` — TRANSFORMATION: Since the query already requires both `t_w_firstyear.year_total > 0` and `t_s_firstyear.year_total > 0`, rewrite the inequality as `w_1999 * s_1998 > s_1999 * w_1998` with the pivoted totals, removing the CASE branches and divisions from the per-row comparison.
